description.text:
SV Chinese Promos holds the promos of the Simplified Chinese game's Scarlet & Violet years, numbered NNN/SV-P. The first, 001 Pikachu, came before the series did: certified shops held viewing events for the 2024 World Championships from 17 to 19 August 2024 and drew one player in eight for it, up to four an event; it carried regulation mark H and could not yet be used at official events. Another Pikachu, marked I, went to winners and lucky players at celebration events for the 2025 World Championships in August and September 2025.

From 21 March 2025 players could earn mission reward packs (任务奖赏包) of one random card by completing tasks in Pokémon China's member mini-program (宝可梦卡牌会员), with a new wave for each booster; from the seventh they hold 12 cards each, and the tenth came with 30th Celebration on 16 September 2026. From 16 January 2026, with Blade Awakening, gyms also give Scarlet & Violet event special packs (活动特别包) and event reward packs (活动奖赏包), again with a new wave for each booster. Each wave of special packs has 30 cards, non-holo cards and Pokémon ex holos, and 25 of them again as Poké Ball and Master Ball pattern holos, packed 89%, 10% and 1% of the time; monthly tasks earn special packs too. Each wave of reward packs holds nine cards.

The official card gyms that Pokémon China opens, many named after a Pokémon, hand out a promo of their Pokémon when they open, while stocks last: Veluza at the Shanghai Wujiaochang gym from 30 October 2025, 35,000 of them, and Klang at the Wuhan Guanggu gym from 3 July 2026, 30,000. Prize cards carry no number: City Leagues give their top eight Poké Ball, and from August 2024 their team events Pal Pad, both marked with the place; Great Ball, marked for the top 64, the top eight, the runner-up or the champion, goes to the best players at Super events such as Wuhan's in May 2025; Rare Candy and three Victory Symbols are marked for the 2025 Guangzhou Masters. Our list numbers the rest up to 434, with gaps, and eight basic Energy print a type code.

description.text: A Simplified Chinese Poké Ball given only as a placement prize at China's City Tournaments (城市赛), in the individual events of both the Standard and the Open format. Each copy is stamped with its placing: Top 8 copies went to players who finished third to eighth, and 2nd Place and Champion copies to the runner-up and the winner.

description.text:
A Simplified Chinese Rare Candy given only as a prize at China's 2025 Master Tournaments (大师赛) in Guangzhou, Hangzhou, Beijing and Shenzhen, each copy stamped with its event and the player's result. The plain event copy went to players with a good record; Top 64, Top 8, 3rd Place, 2nd Place and Champion copies went by final standing, and the top finishers also received a Victory Symbol trophy card.

The Shenzhen Master Tournament was held at the Shenzhen Convention & Exhibition Center on 6 and 7 December 2025, with a team event for its open division.
